programmes.d: In 1999, Patrick McRae was found dead in his Des Moines home and the crime scene was awash with blood. Analysis showed it had come from two people, one of whom was female.
Doctors discover a man's illness is from poison being inflicted by his wife.
A prosecutor helps make video testimony viable in the case of a child's death due to drunk driving.

Two men are murdered while sleeping in their beds. The next night, arson destroys a family planning clinic. Investigators wonder whether some shards of glass, paint chips and a chicken feather could link what appear to be two separate crimes.
When court clerk Peter Porco doesn't report to his work, a courts officer is ordered to his home.
In 2004, Mary Ann Clibbery was found brutally murdered at her Illinois business. Investigators had to determine if this was a robbery gone wrong or a calculated murder.
Eleven-month-old Chad Shelton was admitted to the hospital with unexplained bleeding and later died.

A brilliant young architect falls ill and dies just before she is to testify in a criminal trial. The autopsy reveals she'd been poisoned with arsenic. Investigators must determine who had a motive for murder.
The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage.
Police get a clue about a couple who disappeared on Memorial Day weekend during an in-progress robbery. The evidence found solves a brutal crime.
When Chris Ochoa confessed to the 1988 rape and murder of Nancy DePriest, the case was closed.

In this international case of extortion, murder and stolen identities, scam-artist Albert J. Walker assumes the identity of co-worker Ronald Platt. Platt later turns up dead in an ocean with an anchor tied around his torso.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson returned home after a meeting and discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood. Jack Wilson had obviously been murdered — but how?
A young bride-to-be is gunned down and investigators uncover the man she loved was living a lie.
When a young woman disappears, investigators discover that she led a double life.

A human skeleton was discovered in the North Carolina marshlands. When investigators learned she'd been dead for 18 months, they knew it would be difficult to find out who she was, let alone who killed her.
A fire erupted in Kings Cross Station, killing 31 people and injuring dozens more.

When a popular gym teacher is found dead of what appears to be an accidental gunshot wound, his family is suspicious. A tape recorded by the victim just before his death tells the true story of his strange marriage and his wife's insatiable greed.
An international case of extortion, murder and stolen identities.
A security guard disappeared from his post without a trace; his remains were found a year later in a remote campsite.
Blood splatter evidence contradicts an obstetrician's story who found his wife dead.

In 1988, the body of a young woman was discovered in an Ohio river. Most of the evidence had been washed away, but the victim's 6-year-old son unwittingly told investigators all they needed to know — without saying a word. The clue was in his genes.
911 received a call from a man who said his girlfriend shot herself. The autopsy revealed the truth.
Police investigate a missing college girl and discover her double life: attending school by day and working as a call-girl by night. Her body is found and investigators find her killer.
In 2000, the body of exotic dancer Rachel Siani was found beneath a New Jersey bridge.

Just weeks before a witness is to testify against the man accused of sexually assaulting her, she is murdered in the front yard of her own home. Investigators immediately suspect her attacker, but they don't have enough evidence to prove his guilt.
A teen's role in a high school production of "Hamlet" exposes the truth behind her father's death.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body. Finally, investigators use a single tooth found among some charred remains to identify her.
Two men are convicted of murder after a friend's testimony. Late a bomb kills the witness' father.

Several suspects and conflicting evidence complicated a brutal murder investigation. But the forensics were clear on one thing: the killer knew his victim, and that alone gave investigators a head start.
A shoe impression leads investigators on the right track to finding a killer.

How unlucky could one man be? His college sweetheart killed herself and fourteen years later, his wife ended her life in a similar way. Investigators had to determine if this was murder or simply a bizarre coincidence.
A prosecutor helps make video testimony viable in the case of a child's death due to drunk driving.
In 1996, when a fundamentalist group begins robbing banks near Spokane, authorities know immediately that they are dealing with experienced criminals.
The development of technology could help solve a murder case that is twelve years old.

The murder of an American tourist in a Mexican resort draws law enforcement resources on both sides of the border. At first glance, the motive appears to be robbery, but careful analysis of the forensic evidence points to something more sinister.
A talented television news anchor is shot to death outside her home.

When the wife of a well-known dentist is found dead, police struggle to identify a suspect. Some fibers and a study of the weather patterns on the night of the murder break the case open and reveal the killer.
A behavioral profile caused the Baton Rouge Police Department to search for the wrong man.

A married couple decided to escape the cold of winter with a mini-vacation in Key West. The wife went missing and police searched every square inch of the island; they found nothing but a pair of sandals which might have belonged to her.
When a retired police officer is discovered murdered in his bed, his wife claims it's suicide.

In the series premiere of "Forensic Files", the longest-running true crime series in history, a Connecticut flight attendant goes missing. Police suspect her husband is guilty of murder, but can they prove it?
A woman dies after a long search for medical help in dealing with the side effects of lithium.
In 1991, Dorothy Donovan was murdered in her Dover, Delaware home. When her son stated that she was murdered by a hitchhiker he had picked up, police were skeptical.
During a Christmas party, a young girl disappeared and forensic science is used to solve the case.

One investigator's quick thinking helps him capture a shoe impression made in snow before the evidence melts away. The shoe leads investigators to Peter Benedict and Frank Lanoue, who are convicted of aggravated assault and robbery.
Suspect arrested for drug possession sheds light on a bizarre tale of a stripper's murder case.

A beautiful young woman falls to her death from a cliff overlooking the ocean. Initially, investigators think it was a tragic accident. But after a forensic examination, police uncover a very different picture of what happened.
An infant was rushed to the emergency room with serious breathing problems.
In 1997, Kelly Eckart's car was found, with her belongings still in it, after she worked a late shift in Franklin, Indiana. Days later, her body was found in an isolated ravine.
The apparently motiveless murders of two children baffle police.
On Christmas eve 2005, the corpse of a black male is found burning near Baltimore.

In 2006, Texas real estate agent Sarah Anne Walker was found brutally murdered in a model home. Weeks later, a witness came forward who may have seen the killer. Police used forensic hypnosis to help him recall every detail of the man's appearance.
In 1995, police in San Diego, California are baffled by a pair of hands found in a dumpster.

The body of a young woman was found a mile from her abandoned car. Police were especially concerned when they realized the victim had come to them for protection just two weeks earlier after a road rage incident.
An Alaskan police officer finds a woman's body while on routine patrol of a public park.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later, and witnesses say they saw the victim being forced into a car by an unknown person.
A woman's body is found inside a burned mobile home and the autopsy reveals she was beaten.
When a little girl got sick and died, investigators were stumped. Was it an accident, an unexplained illness or murder?
In 1991, Grand Junction, Colorado is on edge after a series of deadly bombings kill two people.
The crime scene was especially violent: a husband and wife had been shot to death in their bedroom. Was their 16-year-old daughter complicit?

Emergency dispatch received a call from a man who said his girlfriend shot and killed herself. The autopsy revealed that the gunshot wound was not self-inflicted, and the evidence on her body would give police a golden opportunity to catch her killer.
A killer made great effort to obscure the shoe impressions left when he tracked blood on the floor.
Suspect arrested for drug possession sheds light on a bizarre tale of a stripper's murder case.

In 1996, a federal agency ruled that Terri Strickland had intentionally set the fire that killed her 17-month-old son, Josh Hinson. Using the then-emerging resources of the internet, Strickland undertook her own investigation.
Serial killer who hates women, brutally murdered two women who lived in the same apartment complex.

Bombings are difficult to solve because the perpetrator isn't usually at the scene and the evidence goes up in smoke. In this case, pieces of plastic the size of grains of sand hold the key to finding a murderer.
Two suspects are linked to a murder by bloodstained boots and a gun.
The driver said he couldn't have hit and killed a pedestrian on a Harrisburg street. The Jeep Grand Cherokee he was leasing around that time had been sold months ago to a buyer in another state.
A woman's diary helps police piece together the events surrounding her murder.
When more than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984, investigators uncovered a secret plot to influence local elections.
Police are suspicious of a mysterious car crash that kills a young man.

It was one of the most unusual cases in forensic history. Investigators had to find a way to solve a murder case using only a squashed tomato found at the crime scene and tiny, pinpoint reflections of light in a photograph.
A son searches for the truth when his mother is charged with the murder of his father.

The murders of an elderly couple leave police stumped until, two years later, they receive a major break. A jeweler looking through old newspaper clippings recognizes a necklace the female victim wore as having been pawned in her own shop.
For seven years, a trio of men robbed one bank after another.
When a dry cleaner employee is raped and murdered in her store, police turn to forensic science for the answers they need.
A married couple went on a mini-vacation in Key West. But the wife went missing.

In 1994, a human skull retrieved from an Ohio pond reveals a ghastly crime. Markings on the skull indicate that the victim had been stabbed multiple times and that the teeth had been removed with needle-nose pliers.
Janice Johnson was found dead at the foot of her stairs. Was it an accident or murder?
Investigators find a shoe print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints at a murder scene. But they believe the most telling piece of evidence is the bite mark on the victim's chest.
The use of DNA testing helps exonerate a person accused of raping a young Virginia woman.

A two-man shrimp boat sinks when a fast-moving, violent storm strikes the Louisiana coast. The captain drowns, but the deckhand is rescued fourteen hours later. The crewman is hailed as a hero — until the captain's body is discovered.
A murderer eludes the law for years until an age-scaled sculpture helps lead to his arrest.
Even though their daughter had run away before, she had always come back. Her parents were sure this time would be no different, but they were wrong.
Tipster is found dead after revealing that a woman's death 16 years ago was murder.

In the search for the killer of two Texas teenagers, a behavioral profile led to suspect Jason Massey. Hard science proved the profile was correct, and Massey was executed by lethal injection on April 3, 2001.
17-month-old Josh Hinson died in a fire which a federal agency ruled was set by Josh's mother.

When a popular disc jockey was found murdered in a community garden, police swung into action. A sniffer dog and a blood spatter expert led police to the killer, who had been much closer than they realized.
Almost 50 years later, advances in technology identified a murderer who had been free.
Young Navajos in the Southwest were dying at an alarming rate. The tribe's medicine men provided investigators with a critical clue that would lead halfway around the world to a most unlikely killer.
An Alaskan police officer finds a woman's body while on routine patrol of a public park.

When a 9-year-old girl goes missing, police and volunteers spend weeks searching for her. A psychic's vision leads to a field where her body is discovered, along with what investigators hope is enough evidence to find her killer.
In 1984, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned.
Two different men called police to report the same murder. Apparently, neither one knew that the other had called. The investigation uncovered even more unusual circumstances.
Police are led on a wild goose chase when the wife of a prominent banker is kidnapped.

Edward Honaker was convicted of rape, sodomy and aggravated sexual battery and sentenced to three life terms in prison. He maintained his innocence. After years in prison and writing countless letters, he finally found someone who believed him.
A mother's suicide is not convincing when an attempt on her life three years prior is discovered.
In 1989, 4-year-old April Loveless was found dead in the backyard of her Texas home. Her parents told police that she was attacked and killed by wild dogs. Investigators did not agree.
When a retired police officer is discovered murdered in his bed, his wife claims it's suicide.
